newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher on weak U.S. retail sales.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher on weak U.S. retail sales.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late morning Thursday following a rally in U.S. Treasuries after the release of lower than expected May retail sales figures.
"The market is clearly rising on the retail sales," said a trader at a foreign bank.
U.S. retail sales fell 0.1 percent in May against expectations of a 0.4 percent rise, while April retail sales were revised to a 0.9 percent decline from a 0.3 percent fall previously reported.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/4 at 94-1/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.05 at 118.05.
Traders said the U.S. retail figures reduced the chances of a hike in U.S. rates in July.
Players said activity was busy in the morning although another trader said some investors were cautious due to record low Argentine spreads.
